Are there infinitely many $n > 2$ such that $n - 2^k$ is prime for all $k \geq 1$ with $2^k < n$?

The only known such $n$ are $4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105$ (OEIS [A039669](https://oeis.org/A039669)).
references: [Va99] Various, Some of Paul's favorite problems. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
[MiWe69] Mientka, W. E. and Weitzenkamp, R. C., On f-plentiful numbers, Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Volume 7, Issue 4, December 1969, pages 374-377.
